見覚えのある服装。髪型。そう、間違いなく見知
った者の亡骸。
lines.english: Familiar clothes. Familiar hair. Yes—unmistakably the remains of someone she knew.

lines.japanese: 聡明な千鳥は瞬時に悟る。
lines.english: Chidori's keen mind understood at once.

lines.japanese: 貴宮忍―――
lines.english: Shinobu Atemiya—
“…Shino… bu?”

lines.japanese:
伏せた顔面から、おびただしい体液と固形物が広
がっている。
lines.english: A mass of fluid and solid matter spread from the ruined face pressed to the floor.

lines.japanese: そして非人間的に震える四肢。
lines.english: And limbs that trembled with inhuman spasms.

lines.japanese:
カエルの足に電極をとりつけて行う悪趣味な実験
を、千鳥も脈絡なく思い出した。
lines.english: Out of nowhere, Chidori remembered the grotesque experiment in which electrodes were attached to a frog's legs.
“…………Is that… you?”

lines.japanese:
よろめく体を引きずって、忍に取りつく。
　理性は理解している。
　感情が波立っている。
lines.english: Dragging her unsteady body, she clung to Shinobu. Her reason understood. Her emotions churned.

lines.japanese:
そのまま離ればなれになれば楽なのだろう。
　だが冷静さは、二つを強引に結びつけ混じり合わ
せることもある。
lines.english: It might have been easier if the two had simply remained apart. But calm reason could also force them together, binding and mingling them.

lines.japanese: 頭部を銃で撃たれたのだ。
lines.english: He had been shot in the head.

lines.japanese:
これでは、いくらＥＳセルを搭載していても……。
　邑西ほどの専門知識はないものの、ＥＳセルの限
度くらいは知っていた。
lines.english: Even with ES cells inside him, damage like this… She did not possess Yuuzai's expertise, but even she knew the limits of ES cells.

lines.japanese:
治癒、損失部位再生、身体機能強化、細胞補填、
体液補充……人類の平均寿命を１００年は延ばせる
ラインナップだが、残念ながら脳神経組織の再生は
lines.english: Healing, regrowth of lost body parts, enhanced physical function, cellular replacement, replenishment of bodily fluids… The full suite could extend the average human life span by 100 years, but unfortunately it did not include regeneration of

lines.japanese: 含まれない。
lines.english: the brain’s neural tissue.

lines.japanese:
ハードウェアとして、脳の再生だけなら不可能で
はない。
lines.english: Regenerating the brain as mere hardware was not in itself impossible.

lines.japanese:
だとしても……おさめられた記憶までは再生しよ
うがない。
lines.english: Even so… there was no way to regenerate the memories stored within it.

lines.japanese: からっぽの脳だけが蘇生される。
lines.english: Only an empty brain would be revived.

lines.japanese:
何年かの期間さえあれば、能力そのものは保持さ
れるのだから再教育を施すことで……計画に支障は
出ないかも知れない。
lines.english: With a few years to work with, and his abilities still intact, he could be reeducated… Perhaps the plan could proceed without disruption.

lines.japanese:
実際には時間などは残されてはおらず……いや、
そんなことはどうでも良い。
lines.english: In reality, there was no time left… No. None of that mattered.

lines.japanese:
決定された忍の死を前に、千鳥は心を本音が満た
す音を聞いていた。
lines.english: Faced with Shinobu's certain death, Chidori heard the sound of her true feelings filling her heart.

lines.japanese: 長く張りつめた沈黙の末、
lines.english: After a long, taut silence—
“…Ngh!”

lines.japanese: 額を地面に叩きつける勢いで、身体をへし折った。
lines.english: She folded over so violently her forehead nearly struck the floor.
“Oh… Shinobu… Shinobu!”

lines.japanese: 「私の忍が……っ！」
lines.english: “My Shinobu…!”

lines.japanese: 慟哭が、ほとばしる。
lines.english: A wail tore out of her.

lines.japanese: 「いやあぁぁぁぁぁぁぁっ！」
lines.english: “Nooooooooo!”

lines.japanese: 顔を覆う。
lines.english: She covered her face.

lines.japanese:
手塩にかけた。
　育てた。
lines.english: She had tended him with care. Raised him.

lines.japanese:
暮らした。
　重ねた。
lines.english: Lived with him. Built up a life together.

lines.japanese: 今思えば……それは失敗だったのだ。
lines.english: Looking back… that had been her mistake.

lines.japanese:
弟の残骸を差し出して、保持した切り札。
　もともと喜怒哀楽は薄い方だが、感情を懐かない
よう努力してきた。
lines.english: A trump card preserved at the cost of her brother's remains. She had never been prone to strong emotion, but even so she had worked to keep herself from growing attached.

lines.japanese:
気にすれば、弟の名を与えたこの献体を、憎んで
しまうおそれがあったからだ。
lines.english: If she allowed herself to care, she feared she might come to hate the experimental subject to whom she had given her brother's name.

lines.japanese:
実際は、逆だった。
　模倣子の影響下から逃れている千鳥でさえ、自身
の感情だけはどうしようもない。
lines.english: In truth, the opposite had happened. Even Chidori, who had escaped the mimetic unit's influence, was powerless against her own feelings.

lines.japanese: 何年も、過ごしたのだ。
lines.english: They had spent years together.

lines.japanese: 友を持ち、忍は色づいていった。
lines.english: Shinobu had made friends, and color had entered him.

lines.japanese:
機械のようだったのに、気がつけば薄桃色の少年
へと育まれていた。
lines.english: He had once been like a machine; before she knew it, he had grown into a boy touched with pale rose.

lines.japanese:
千鳥が育てたわけではない。
　だとしても、二人の距離は錯覚を招くほどに、近
かった。
lines.english: Chidori had not raised him. Even so, they had grown close enough to invite the illusion that she had.

lines.japanese:
そして忍は、組織からの指示にさえ反抗する覚悟
で……友を選んだ。
lines.english: And Shinobu had chosen his friends… prepared even to defy the organization's orders.

lines.japanese:
計画からすれば、あってはならない事態。
　だとしても千鳥は、嬉しかった。
lines.english: Under the plan, it was an impermissible development. Even so, Chidori had been glad.

lines.japanese:
真意は漏れ、ぎこちない二人は、ぎこちない仕方
で和解した。
lines.english: The truth had slipped out, and the awkward pair had reconciled in their own awkward way.

lines.japanese:
関係がどう変わるわけではない。
　忍の大事にしている領域に、自分が入ったという
感覚もない。
lines.english: It had not transformed their relationship. She had no sense that she had entered the territory of his life he held dear.

lines.japanese:
ただ以前より少しだけ近づいて、新しい関係性を
―――
lines.english: They had only drawn a little closer than before, beginning to form something new—

lines.japanese:
だが、すでに開戦準備段階。
　二人は新たな距離感をはかる前に、微量の感情を
胸に、情感を放棄しなければならなかった。
lines.english: But preparations for war were already underway. Before they could measure the new distance between them, they had to keep those faint feelings in their hearts and cast emotion aside.

lines.japanese: 「う、うっうっ、うっ……こんな、こんなっ……」
lines.english: “Hh… hh… hh… This… This…”

lines.japanese:
掌で押さえつけた双眼から、こんこんと涙がこぼ
れていく。柄にもない。
lines.english: Tears welled endlessly from the eyes beneath her palms. It was wholly unlike her.

lines.japanese: 喪った悲しみが、弟の分と重なっている。
lines.english: Her grief for this loss overlapped with her grief for her brother.

lines.japanese:
冷血の防壁を突き破る、大質量の感情。
　この事件は、貴宮千鳥という人格を使いものにな
らなくするほどのものだった。
lines.english: A vast mass of emotion broke through her cold-blooded defenses. This incident was enough to render the personality called Chidori Atemiya unusable.

lines.japanese: でも、大丈夫。
lines.english: But it was all right.
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
弾かれたように、顔をあげた。
　何もいない。いるはずがない。
　ちょうど殺害者が去って、三分が経過していた。
lines.english: Her head snapped up. No one was there. No one could have been. Exactly three minutes had passed since the killer's departure.

lines.japanese: 頃合いである。
lines.english: The time was right.

lines.japanese: 処理―――開始
lines.english: Process—begin

lines.japanese:
細胞が加熱する。
　破損部位を中心に、細胞分裂が促される。
lines.english: The cells grew hot. Cell division accelerated around the damaged areas.

lines.japanese: そして体内の眠れる巨人・ＥＳセルが身をもたげる。
lines.english: And the sleeping giant within his body—the ES cells—began to stir.

lines.japanese:
細胞損失箇所伝達。効率化。
　万能細胞全起動。
lines.english: Transmit sites of cellular loss. Optimize. Activate all pluripotent cells.

lines.japanese:
かつて邑西らが投入した初期型のＥＳセルとは別
物のそれは……忍を怪物と呼ばれるに足るものに変
えている。
lines.english: They were nothing like the early ES cells once implanted by Yuuzai and the others… They had transformed Shinobu into something worthy of being called a monster.

lines.japanese:
忍さえ知らないところで、進化は促された。
　時間をかけて育て上げた。
lines.english: Without Shinobu's knowledge, their evolution had been fostered. They had been cultivated over time.

lines.japanese:
時に必要に迫られ、時に暇つぶし、時に自分を守
るため。
lines.english: At times from necessity, at times to pass the time, and at times to protect himself.

lines.japanese: 貴宮忍という個体はリジェネートを研鑽していった。
lines.english: The individual known as Shinobu Atemiya had honed Regenerate.

lines.japanese:
今はただ、貴宮忍だけが行使できる。
　忍の全身から、白煙が立ちのぼる。
　再生熱による現象である。
lines.english: Now Shinobu Atemiya alone could wield it. White vapor rose from every inch of his body. It was a product of the heat of regeneration.
“…Shi… nobu?”

lines.japanese:
固唾を呑んで、千鳥は見つめる。
　彼女から見ても、信じがたい光景である。
　高度に発達した化学は魔法そのものだ。
lines.english: Chidori held her breath and watched. Even to her, the sight was unbelievable. Highly advanced chemistry was magic itself.

lines.japanese:
骨はあとで再生すればいい。
　なくとも、細胞を硬質化させて補える。
lines.english: Bone could be regenerated later. Until then, hardened cells could serve in its place.

lines.japanese:
破片が残っている部分については、それを癒着さ
せて文字通り骨材にする。
lines.english: Where fragments remained, the cells fused them together and used them quite literally as aggregate.

lines.japanese:
脳内の羊水を満たすには、少なくなった体液を搾
り取る必要がある。
lines.english: To refill the amniotic fluid within the brain, what little bodily fluid remained would have to be wrung out.

lines.japanese: が、それだけでは足りない。
lines.english: But that would not be enough.

lines.japanese:
大気中から取り込むことにした。
　模倣子のうねり。
　幸い、空調は回っている。
lines.english: It would be drawn from the atmosphere. A swell of mimetic units. Fortunately, the ventilation system was running.

lines.japanese:
運ばれてくる微生物たちが、マテリアルとなって
蘇生を加速する。
lines.english: The microorganisms it carried became raw material, accelerating resuscitation.

lines.japanese:
脳の再生は順調だ。
　記憶はどうするのか？
lines.english: The brain's regeneration proceeded smoothly. But what of the memories?

lines.japanese: 決まっていた。
lines.english: The answer had been decided.

lines.japanese:
まっさらではない、記憶を保持した状態の脳とし
て蘇生するのだ。
lines.english: The brain would be revived not as a blank slate, but with its memories intact.

lines.japanese: 同期情報再入力―――
lines.english: Re-enter synchronized data—

lines.japanese:
造形を取り戻しつつ、意識の修復に入る。
　外部記憶領域から、再生された脳内に情報を格納
していく。
lines.english: As the structure regained its form, repair of consciousness began. Information was transferred from external memory and stored in the regenerated brain.

lines.japanese:
千鳥はもはや、息を詰めて見守っている。
　眼前の出来事は、彼女の想像を超えている。
lines.english: By now, Chidori was watching with bated breath. What unfolded before her surpassed anything she had imagined.

lines.japanese:
顔面修復終了。
　色素を操作し、生まれたばかりでピンク色の細胞
に肌色の化粧を施す。
lines.english: Facial restoration complete. Pigmentation was adjusted, giving the newly formed pink cells a skin-colored coating.

lines.japanese: 同時に、後頭部側の穴を埋めにかかる。
lines.english: At the same time, the opening at the back of the skull began to close.

lines.japanese: 脳内をカッティングした弾丸の破片除去。
lines.english: Removing the bullet fragments that had cut through the brain.

lines.japanese:
筋肉ならびに細胞ペーストの流動によって実行……
終了。
lines.english: Executed through the movement of muscle and cellular paste… Complete.

lines.japanese: 胴体内部損傷修復……終了。
lines.english: Repair of internal torso damage… complete.

lines.japanese:
銃弾侵入と同時にＥＳセルが緊縮し臓器をスライド
させたため、損害度合いについて特記事項なし。
lines.english: Upon bullet penetration, the ES cells contracted and displaced the organs; degree of damage therefore presents no exceptional concerns.

lines.japanese: 全身体部位完全再生―――完了
lines.english: Complete regeneration of all body parts—complete

lines.japanese: 意識情報再インストール―――完了
lines.english: Reinstallation of consciousness data—complete

lines.japanese: 貴宮忍、再起動―――
lines.english: Shinobu Atemiya—rebooting

lines.japanese: どれほどの時間がかかっただろう。
lines.english: How much time had passed?

lines.japanese:
少年は身を起こす。
　熱の冷却がまだ終わっていないため、身体にだる
さがある。
lines.english: The boy pushed himself upright. The heat had not yet finished dissipating, leaving his body heavy and sluggish.
“Mm…”

lines.japanese:
目が開かない。
　まぶたの下で、眼球がぐるぐると動き回っている。
lines.english: His eyes would not open. Beneath the lids, his eyeballs rolled wildly.

lines.japanese: （そうか……再生……機能したんだ）
lines.english: (I see… Regeneration… It worked.)

lines.japanese:
ゆっくりと、まぶたを持ち上げた。
　千鳥がそこにいた。
　ぼやけた顔。
lines.english: Slowly, he raised his eyelids. Chidori was there. Her face was a blur.

lines.japanese:
一秒。
　鮮明なものになる。
　彼女は泣いていた。
lines.english: One second. It sharpened into focus. She was crying.

lines.japanese: 「……ねえ、さん？」

主任とは言えなかった。
　泣いている顔を見てしまったから。
lines.english: He could not call her Chief. Not after seeing her face in tears.

lines.japanese:
雛が親鳥を見るように。
　生まれなおしたばかりの忍は、姉と呼べる者を
見た。
lines.english: Like a chick looking at its parent. Newly born again, Shinobu looked at the person he could call his sister.
“…Shinobu!”

lines.japanese:
そっと抱きしめる。
　できたばかりの頭が、潰れてしまわないように。
lines.english: She embraced him gently. Careful not to crush his newly formed head.

lines.japanese: 「姉さん……」
lines.english: “Sis…”

lines.japanese:
眼球再生の過程で生じた汚水は、大量の涙液によ
って稀釈され、体外に排出。
lines.english: The fouled water produced during the regeneration of his eyes was diluted by copious tears and expelled from the body.

lines.japanese:
機械的に流れる廃涙は、しかし懐かしい匂いに抱
きしめられて、次第にその純度を高めていった。
lines.english: Those waste tears flowed mechanically. Yet held in a familiar scent, they gradually grew purer.

lines.japanese: そんな気が、忍はしたのだ―――
lines.english: Or so it seemed to Shinobu—

lines.japanese:
廊下を歩く。
　もはや、横たわる骸は現実のものだ。
　見えてはいるが、視線を向けもせず、忍は歩く。
lines.english: He walked down the corridor. The corpses on the floor were real to him now. He saw them, but walked on without looking their way.

lines.japanese: 焦燥が少年を突き動かす。
lines.english: Urgency drove the boy onward.

lines.japanese: （……こんなに……殺されている）
lines.english: (…So many… murdered.)

lines.japanese:
高度な訓練を受けたＵＳＥＲは、開戦時には欠く
ことのできない重要ノードである。
lines.english: A highly trained USER was an indispensable node once the war began.

lines.japanese:
どれほどの損害が出たのか、何人の端末が失われ
たのか。
lines.english: How great were the losses? How many terminals had been lost?

lines.japanese:
忍はすでに、イマジナリー・ネットから破損端末
を割り出している。
lines.english: Shinobu had already identified the damaged terminals through the Imaginary Net.

hyperlinks.preview: Also known as the Chemical Network (CN) or the Imaginary Network (IN).

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: Also known as the Chemical Network (CN) or the Imaginary Network (IN).

lines.japanese:
もともと施設にいた者のうち、ＩＰ反応が消失し
たままのスタッフ数は……２０を超えていた。
　手痛い損害と言えた。
lines.english: Of those originally present at the facility, the number of staff whose IP signatures remained absent… exceeded 20. A grievous loss.

lines.japanese: （愚かな、ことを）
lines.english: (What folly.)

lines.japanese:
もともとなかった勝率が、さらに削られたような
ものだ。
lines.english: It was as though their already nonexistent chance of victory had been whittled down still further.

lines.japanese: なのに、灰野を追わねばならなかった。
lines.english: Even so, he had to pursue Haino.

lines.japanese: （追尾は……拒否）
lines.english: (Tracking request… denied.)

lines.japanese: ＧＶＰの原理上、忍の要請が拒否されることはない。
lines.english: Under the principles of the GVP, no request from Shinobu should ever be denied.

lines.japanese: （……どういうことだろう）
lines.english: (…What does this mean?)

lines.japanese: 忍の知らない真実が、まだ隠されているのだろうか。
lines.english: Was there still some truth being kept from Shinobu?

lines.japanese:
そうとしか考えられず、またそう考えるべきであ
った。
lines.english: No other explanation came to mind—and it was the conclusion he ought to draw.

lines.japanese: （確かめるには……彼本人に問いかけるしかない）
lines.english: (To find out… I'll have to ask the man himself.)

lines.japanese: 検知できなくても、手段はある。
lines.english: Even if he could not detect the man directly, other means remained.

lines.japanese:
並列処理による情報伝達速度の最適化。
　思考力が加速。
　蘇生したばかりの細胞が熱い。
lines.english: Parallel processing optimized the speed of information transfer. His thoughts accelerated. The newly revived cells burned hot.

lines.japanese:
熱病のようだ。
　だが……王の力は寸分たりとも損なわれてはいない。
lines.english: Like a raging fever. But… not the slightest measure of the king's power had been lost.

lines.japanese:
おおよそ人類で、忍に抗しうる人間はいない。
　忍はすでに、人類の敵の、そのもっとも下等な領域
に位置している。
lines.english: Virtually no human being could stand against Shinobu. Shinobu already occupied the lowest stratum among humanity's enemies.

lines.japanese: （同じ人類でありながら、手こずる）
lines.english: (And yet another human gives me this much trouble.)

lines.japanese: 掻痒感。不安。波状に飛来する赤い感情。怒り。
lines.english: An itch. Anxiety. A red emotion sweeping in waves. Anger.

lines.japanese:
煩わしかった。
　冷静さを取り戻すため、忍はトランキライザーを
処方した。
lines.english: It was tiresome. To regain his composure, Shinobu prescribed himself a tranquilizer.

lines.japanese: 瞬時に、苛立ちは抑制された。
lines.english: His irritation was suppressed at once.
“Shinobu!”

lines.japanese: 壁に手をついて、南が歩いてきた。
lines.english: Minami came toward him, one hand braced against the wall.

lines.japanese: 「南、生存者の情報は？」
lines.english: “Minami, what do we know about the survivors?”

lines.japanese:
「受け取った。
　だが内線が切られていて……効率が悪い」
lines.english: “I got it. But the internal lines are down… Not very efficient.”

lines.japanese:
「死ぬ者は死ぬ。助からない者は……三人ほどいる
　な。悪いけど。彼らを救助している時間はない」
lines.english: “Those who die, die. There are… about three who can't be saved. Sorry, but we don't have time to rescue them.”

lines.japanese: 「更新しようか―――」
lines.english: “Let's update that—”

lines.japanese: 更新。
lines.english: Update.

lines.japanese:
「―――そのうち二名は、もう一分以内に。
　残った一名はあと７、６―――」
lines.english: “—Two of them will be gone within the next minute. The last has 7, 6—”

lines.japanese: 「やめてくれ」
lines.english: “Stop.”

lines.japanese:
絞り出すような声だった。
　南にとっては手塩にかけた部下たちだ。
　独立愚連隊と呼ばれてきた。
lines.english: The word came out strangled. Minami had personally trained and cared for those subordinates. They had long been known as a maverick outfit.

lines.japanese:
忍にとっては、部品でしかない彼らも、南にとっ
ては血の通った仲間なのだ。
　人類最高の現象行使者の額に、深い皺が刻まれた。
lines.english: To Shinobu they were no more than parts. To Minami, they were flesh-and-blood comrades. Deep creases scored the brow of humanity's greatest wielder of phenomena.

lines.japanese: 「他は……ほっといても命に別状はない……んだな」
lines.english: “The others… Their lives aren't in danger if we leave them… right?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese:
「沢野が無事なんだったな。あいつに伝達できれば、
　そのあたりはうまく―――」
lines.english: “Sawano made it, didn't he? If we can get word to him, he should be able to handle—”

lines.japanese: 「伝えておくよ」
lines.english: “I'll tell him.”

lines.japanese:
忍は、彼だけが用いることのできる機能……
有機メールを送信した。
lines.english: Shinobu used a function available to him alone… He sent a message by organic mail.

hyperlinks.preview: The power to force a message through to another person. Ordinarily, primitive telepathy cannot easil

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: The power to force a message through to another person. Ordinarily, primitive telepathy cannot easil

lines.japanese: 「開封確認。沢野に命令は転送されたよ」
lines.english: “Read receipt confirmed. The orders have been forwarded to Sawano.”

lines.japanese: 「……防壁は関係なく届くんだな」
lines.english: “…It gets through regardless of the barrier.”

lines.japanese: 「そうでなければ、軍用とは言えない」
lines.english: “It wouldn't qualify as military-grade if it didn't.”

lines.japanese:
「だけどおかしい。あの灰野って男……どこにいる
　かわからない。情報もない。イマジナリー・ネット
　には、彼の情報がまるでない」
lines.english: “But something's wrong. That man Haino… I can't tell where he is. There's no data. The Imaginary Net contains absolutely nothing about him.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「おかしい。変だ。何か、あるんだ」
lines.english: “This isn't right. It's strange. There's something behind this.”

lines.japanese:
「僕はやる。決めたんだ。これ以上、人類同士で摩耗
　している場合じゃない」
lines.english: “I'm doing it. I've decided. This is no time for humanity to keep wearing itself down fighting itself.”

lines.japanese: 「直接、捕捉して排除するつもりだよ」
lines.english: “I mean to locate him directly and eliminate him.”

lines.japanese: 「居場所は？」
lines.english: “Where is he?”

lines.japanese:
「……僕の機能で瞬間的にキャッチできないだけで、
　時間をかければ方法はあるよ。物理的な手段だっ
　て、あるしね」
lines.english: “…My functions simply can't pick him up instantaneously. Given enough time, I have other options. Physical ones, too.”

lines.japanese: 「すぐに動くのか？」
lines.english: “Are you moving now?”

lines.japanese: 低い声で、忍は言った。
lines.english: Shinobu answered in a low voice.

lines.japanese: 「もう、動いているよ」
lines.english: “I'm already moving.”

lines.japanese: 廊下にある内線が、コール音を発した。
lines.english: An internal phone in the corridor began to ring.

lines.japanese: 「復旧されたか……」
lines.english: “They got it working again…”

lines.japanese: 取り上げる。
lines.english: He picked it up.

lines.japanese: 「南だ……なに？」
lines.english: “Minami here… What?”

lines.japanese: 忍を見やって、
lines.english: He looked toward Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 「森に向かう車を見つけた、と言っている」
lines.english: “They say they've spotted a vehicle heading for the forest.”

lines.japanese: 「追尾してもらって」
lines.english: “Have them follow it.”

lines.japanese: 「誰なんだ、これは？」
lines.english: “Who is this?”

lines.japanese:
「向こうさんの通信スタッフと、ヘリの乗員だよ。
　協力してもらってる」
lines.english: “Their communications staff and the helicopter crew. They're helping us.”
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
「常備隊の隊員さんたちだね。困ったことに、何も
　知らないまま作戦に引っ張り出されたらしいよ」
lines.english: “They're with the standing force. Unfortunately, it seems they were dragged into this operation without being told a thing.”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ、行ってくる。
　南も手当を受けた方がいいよ」
lines.english: “All right, I'm going. You should get treated too, Minami.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、別状はない。俺も同行する」
lines.english: “No, it's nothing serious. I'm coming with you.”

lines.japanese: 「え、来るの？」
lines.english: “Huh? You are?”

lines.japanese:
「……俺は、おまえを護衛しなければならない
　からな」
lines.english: “…I have to serve as your bodyguard, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、いいけど」
lines.english: “Fine by me.”

lines.japanese:
肩をすくめ、一人で歩き出す。
　南があとに従った。
lines.english: He shrugged and set off on his own. Minami followed.

lines.japanese:
草原に出ると、例の輸送ヘリが飛行可能状態で待
機していた。
lines.english: When they emerged into the grasslands, the same transport helicopter stood ready for flight.

lines.japanese: 「偵察ヘリじゃなかったんだ？」
lines.english: “Not the scout helicopter?”

lines.japanese: 「あれは二人乗りです」
lines.english: “That one only seats two.”

lines.japanese: 敬礼をしたままで、隊員は告げた。
lines.english: The soldier answered without lowering his salute.

lines.japanese: 「そう。じゃ森まで頼むよ」
lines.english: “I see. Then take us to the forest.”

lines.japanese: 「１０分もかかりません」
lines.english: “It won't take 10 minutes.”

lines.japanese: 「行こう、南」
lines.english: “Let's go, Minami.”
“R-right…”

lines.japanese: 敵方の常備隊が、なぜ忍の指揮系統にあるのか。
lines.english: Why was the enemy standing force now under Shinobu's command?

lines.japanese:
南は混乱を抱えたまま、敵機の胎におさまること
になった。
lines.english: Still bewildered, Minami found himself inside the belly of the enemy aircraft.

lines.japanese:
離陸。
　双発ローターが、機体を軽々と持ち上げる。
　滑るように、進む。
lines.english: Takeoff. The twin rotors lifted the airframe with ease. It glided forward.

lines.japanese:
速い。
　鈍重な印象があるが、決してそんなことはなかった。
lines.english: Fast. It looked ponderous, but was anything but.

lines.japanese:
町内だ。
　言葉通り、すぐにつくだろう。
　いろいろな疑問があった。
lines.english: The destination was within town limits. They should arrive soon, just as the soldier had said. Minami had many questions.

lines.japanese: だが南はそのうちの一つだけを、持ち出した。
lines.english: But he voiced only one of them.

lines.japanese: 「……自分でやるつもりか？」
lines.english: “…You’re planning to do it yourself?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。得体が知れないから」
lines.english: “Yes. Because I don't know what he is.”

lines.japanese: 「……それと、これをもって決意としたいから」
lines.english: “…And because I want this to mark my resolve.”

lines.japanese: 「何の？」
lines.english: “Your resolve to do what?”

lines.japanese: 重い沈黙。だが、意図的に閉ざされた唇である。
lines.english: A heavy silence. But he was deliberately keeping his lips sealed.

lines.japanese: 南はそこに、うそ寒い重圧を感じた。
lines.english: Minami felt a chilling pressure in that silence.

lines.japanese:
―――その日が、革命を目論んだ男の最後の日だ
った。
lines.english: —That was the final day of the man who had plotted a revolution.

hyperlinks.preview: Haino

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: Haino

lines.japanese:
忍は空を見る。いつものように。
　正常な空。健康な空だ。
lines.english: Shinobu looked at the sky, as he always did. A normal sky. A healthy sky.

lines.japanese:
空の向こうに、忌まわしいものがあるとは考えた
くはない。
lines.english: He did not want to imagine anything hateful lurking beyond that sky.

lines.japanese: 空気がなくなれば、空の青みが失われるとも。
lines.english: Nor that if the air vanished, the sky would lose its blue.

lines.japanese:
青の崩壊などは悪夢でしかない。
　忍の中では、そう決められていた。
lines.english: The collapse of blue could be nothing but a nightmare. That much was settled in Shinobu’s mind.

lines.japanese:
草原で一人見上げていると、罪と罰をたぐり寄せ
てしまう。
lines.english: Alone in the grass, gazing up, he found his thoughts turning to sin and punishment.

lines.japanese: 思考は堂々巡り。結論を導かない。
lines.english: His thoughts ran in circles, reaching no conclusion.

lines.japanese:
結局のところ、忍にとって罪とは侵害であり、聖
域は最上の価値を有するものであった。
lines.english: In the end, to Shinobu, sin was violation, while the sanctuary held supreme value.

lines.japanese: 聖域は心であることが多い。
lines.english: Most often, that sanctuary was the heart.

lines.japanese:
家族、恋人、夫婦、兄弟姉妹、仲間……共有幻想
は過去のものだ。
lines.english: Family, lovers, married couples, siblings, comrades… such shared illusions belonged to the past.

lines.japanese:
うち捨てられた廃墟であり、そこに住まうのは哀
れな物乞いである。
lines.english: They were abandoned ruins, inhabited only by pitiable beggars.

lines.japanese: 同意なき干渉は罪である。
lines.english: Interference without consent was sin.

lines.japanese:
ゆえに全ての親は罪人である。
　子を教育するからだ。
　子を教育しない者は外道であり、やはり罪人だ。
lines.english: Therefore, every parent was a sinner. Because they taught their children. Those who did not were monsters—and sinners all the same.

lines.japanese:
自己矛盾から人は逃れることはできない。
　もっとも正しき行いは、孤立することである。
　鋭く、貴く、厳しく、甘く。
lines.english: No person could escape self-contradiction. The most righteous course was isolation. Sharp, noble, severe, and sweet.

lines.japanese:
部屋に籠もる者こそ、圧倒的に正しい。
　なぜなら誰にも直接的影響を与えないからだ。
lines.english: Those who shut themselves away in their rooms were overwhelmingly in the right. For they exerted no direct influence on anyone.

lines.japanese: 心を共有することは、少人数に限り成立するだろう。
lines.english: Hearts could perhaps be shared, but only among a handful of people.

lines.japanese:
人類は一つにはならない。メディアの力をもって
しても。
lines.english: Humanity would not become one. Not even through the power of media.

lines.japanese: 無数の聖域が在るばかり。
lines.english: There were only countless sanctuaries.

lines.japanese:
結束がないそれらは、弱い。
　未成熟で、青く、幼く、たおやかな生命相。
　現段階における人類の限界点でもある。
lines.english: Without unity, they were weak. An immature, blue, childlike, supple phase of life. The limit of what humanity could achieve at present.

lines.japanese: （なら……それでいいじゃないか）
lines.english: (Then… what's wrong with that?)

lines.japanese: と思う。
lines.english: That was what he thought.

lines.japanese:
膝を抱えて、ぼんやりと時間を過ごす。
　と、まるで日課のように、南がやってくる。
　いつものことだ。
lines.english: He clasped his knees and let time pass in a haze. Then, as though it were part of the daily routine, Minami arrived. The usual thing.

lines.japanese: 「おまえは、ここが好きだな」
lines.english: “You really do like this place.”

lines.japanese: 「一人でいるのが好きだから」
lines.english: “Because I like being alone.”

lines.japanese: 口調が平坦なことが、かえって南を不安にさせた。
lines.english: The very flatness of his tone made Minami uneasy.

lines.japanese: 「……怒っているのか？」
lines.english: “…Are you angry?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 言われて、はじめて忍は自分の表情に気づく。
lines.english: Only when Minami said it did Shinobu notice his own expression.

lines.japanese: 「いや、そんなこともないけど……」
lines.english: “No, not really…”

lines.japanese:
険しい面持ちの名残で、目元が軽く疲労をうった
えている。
lines.english: A trace of that grim expression lingered, leaving a faint weariness around his eyes.

lines.japanese: 「なら、いいが」
lines.english: “Good, then.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、どうなんだろう」
lines.english: “Still, I wonder.”

lines.japanese: 曇り、次いで憂色をたたえる。
lines.english: His face clouded, then filled with melancholy.

lines.japanese: 「いろいろ考えてると、気分が重くなってさ」
lines.english: “The more I think about everything, the heavier I feel.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうタイプには見えないな」
lines.english: “You don't strike me as the type.”

lines.japanese: 「ひどいな」
lines.english: “That's cruel.”

lines.japanese:
無理して笑う。
　ああ、無理して笑うという行為そのものが、事務
的であり自動的である。
lines.english: He forced a smile. Ah. Even forcing a smile had become perfunctory, automatic.

lines.japanese: 「南には、いい部下がたくさんいるね」
lines.english: “You have a lot of good people under you, Minami.”

lines.japanese: 「……ああ。よくやってくれている」
lines.english: “…Yes. They've served me well.”

lines.japanese:
「皆、ネット全体の接続状態が、格段に良くなった
　と言っていた。これもおまえの力なのか？」
lines.english: “Everyone says connections across the network are far better now. Is that your power too?”

lines.japanese: 「もともと、そのための力なんだ」
lines.english: “That's what this power was for in the first place.”

lines.japanese:
「今までは、断片的だったり時間制限があったり能
　力に左右されたりして、なかなか不便なものだっ
　たのだがな。段違いだ」
lines.english: “Until now it was fragmentary, time-limited, and dependent on the user's ability—hardly convenient. This is in another league.”

lines.japanese: 「APOPの方は？」
lines.english: “How is APOP?”

lines.japanese: 「良好だ」
lines.english: “Working well.”

lines.japanese:
「セキュリティも万全で安心して用いることができ
　る。通常の感応通信と比べると、使い勝手は格段
　に上だ」
lines.english: “The security is airtight, so we can use it with confidence. Compared with ordinary telepathic communication, it is vastly more practical.”

lines.japanese: 「解放した甲斐があったよ」
lines.english: “Then opening it up was worthwhile.”

lines.japanese: 「だが……いいのか？」
lines.english: “But… is that all right?”

lines.japanese: 「何が？」
lines.english: “Is what all right?”

lines.japanese: 「これは王だけが用いる伝達機能だったはずだ」
lines.english: “That transmission function was supposed to be reserved for the king.”

lines.japanese:
「いいんだよ。僕のメールは優先権があるし、普段
　君たちが使ったところで支障はない」
lines.english: “It's fine. My messages have priority, and your everyday use won't interfere with anything.”

lines.japanese:
「第一、相手のアドレスを知らなかったら、君たち
　は送信できないようにしてある。問題は起こらな
　いと思う」
lines.english: “Besides, I've made it so you can't send anything unless you know the recipient's address. I don't think there'll be any trouble.”

lines.japanese: 「沢野が、おまえを評価していた」
lines.english: “Sawano spoke highly of you.”

lines.japanese:
「王様もちょっとは自分たちのこと考えてくれてる
　んだな、と」
lines.english: “He said, 'Guess His Majesty does give some thought to us after all.'”

lines.japanese: 「単純だ」
lines.english: “Simple-minded.”

lines.japanese: 苦笑する。
lines.english: He gave a wry smile.

lines.japanese: 「そう言うな」
lines.english: “Don't say that.”

lines.japanese: 心当たりがあるのか、南もぎこちなく微笑した。
lines.english: Perhaps the comment struck home; Minami smiled awkwardly too.

lines.japanese:
ぎこちなく……少年らしい振るまいを知らないか
のように。
lines.english: Awkwardly… as if he did not know how a boy was supposed to behave.

lines.japanese: 「僕はそんな人じゃないよ」
lines.english: “I'm not that kind of person.”

lines.japanese: 「悪党だ」
lines.english: “I'm a villain.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえのどこが悪党なんだ」
lines.english: “What makes you a villain?”

lines.japanese:
「君はさ、これから起こることが何か、見当もつか
　ないの？」
lines.english: “You really have no idea what's about to happen, do you?”

lines.japanese: 言葉には苛立ちが混じる。わずか。
lines.english: A trace of irritation colored the words.

lines.japanese: 「それを、悪と言わずどうするのかって話でさ」
lines.english: “If that isn't evil, what is? That's what I'm saying.”

lines.japanese:
「しかし必要があってのことだろう？　俺たちには
　できないことだし、できる立場の者がやるのは当
　然で」
lines.english: “But it’s necessary, isn’t it? We can’t do it. Surely the person in a position to do it should—”

lines.japanese: 「どんな必然がそうさせても、責任はあるよ」
lines.english: “Whatever makes it necessary, you’re still responsible.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、責任の質の話ってことになるのかな」
lines.english: “So I suppose the question is what kind of responsibility it is.”

lines.japanese:
「考えすぎだ。おまえはそのために調整されたし、
　人類の誰だっておまえを責める権利なんて―――」
lines.english: “You think too much. You were engineered for this, and no one in humanity has any right to blame you—”

lines.japanese: 「あるさ」
lines.english: “They do.”

lines.japanese: 遮って、言う。
lines.english: He cut Minami off.

lines.japanese:
「自分のしていることが、どんな結果に繋がるのか
　知っているからね」
lines.english: “Because I know what consequences my actions will bring.”

lines.japanese:
「おまえは正しいはずだ。そうでなければ、誰が、
　何が、良い行いになると言うんだ？」
lines.english: “You must be in the right. If not, then who—what—could ever be called good?”

lines.japanese: しかし南は食い下がる。
lines.english: But Minami would not yield.

lines.japanese:
本音の証か。
　表情には微量の憤り。
lines.english: Proof that he meant it, perhaps. A trace of indignation showed on his face.

lines.japanese:
「人は狭いよ。何も許しはしないさ。合一もできな
　い。ただ共感して共有するだけだ。それだって、
　世界規模では起こらない。相反しているからだ」
lines.english: “People are narrow. They forgive nothing. They cannot unite. They can only empathize and share—and even that won't happen on a global scale, because they stand opposed.”

lines.japanese:
「人種、理念、言葉、印象……ありとあらゆる場所
　に、反目の種があるんだ」
lines.english: “Race, ideology, language, impressions… The seeds of antagonism are everywhere.”

lines.japanese:
「たまたま人類全てが互いに許し合えるなんて、どれ
　だけ時を重ねても起こりえない。確率の上ではある
　かも知れない。けど、それこそ絵空事だ」
lines.english: “The whole of humanity will never just happen to forgive one another, no matter how much time passes. It may be possible in terms of probability, but it's still a fantasy.”

lines.japanese:
「たまたま全人類が互いを全肯定できる瞬間なんての
　はね、宇宙と同じ広さの空間を飛ぶ二匹の蜂がさ、
　衝突するのと同じくらい起こりえないことだよ」
lines.english: “A moment when all humanity just happens to affirm one another completely is about as likely as two bees colliding in a space as vast as the universe.”

lines.japanese: 「だけど、それを否定しているんじゃない」
lines.english: “But I'm not denying that possibility.”

lines.japanese:
「ただ、人はそういう性質のものだって、わかるん
　だよ」
lines.english: “I simply understand that this is what human beings are like.”

lines.japanese:
「９９％の孤独と１％の共感で、生きていくものな
　んだ」
lines.english: “They live on 99 percent solitude and 1 percent empathy.”

lines.japanese: 風が低く滑って、草むらを撫で、空気をかきまぜる。
lines.english: The wind skimmed low, stroking the grass and stirring the air.

lines.japanese:
「世界はさ、俗人の愚かしいうねりで動いていくん
　じゃないか」
lines.english: “Isn't the world driven by the foolish tide of ordinary people?”

lines.japanese:
「一部の天才だけが世界を動かしている……なんて
　迷信を、君まで信じているわけじゃないだろ？」
lines.english: “You don't believe that superstition too, do you—that only a handful of geniuses move the world?”

lines.japanese: 「……そうだな」

この３５年こそ、俗人が一部の天才を翻弄し、発
狂へと至らしめた経緯であったのだ。
lines.english: Those 35 years were the story of ordinary people buffeting a handful of geniuses until they went mad.

lines.japanese: 第一次敷設計画―――
lines.english: The First Deployment Plan—

lines.japanese: ＷＨＯ指導のもとで実施された抗環境ホルモン計画。
lines.english: An anti-endocrine-disruptor program conducted under WHO direction.

hyperlinks.preview: World Health Organization

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: World Health Organization

lines.japanese:
同計画を隠れ蓑とし、先進国を中心に世界２４７
箇所の人口過密地帯で実施された。
lines.english: Using that program as cover, it was implemented at 247 densely populated sites around the world, chiefly in developed nations.

lines.japanese:
が、配布された薬剤に微生物混入の事実が公表・
指摘され、世界的な非難を浴びた。
lines.english: But when it came to light that the distributed drugs had been contaminated with microorganisms, the program drew worldwide condemnation.

lines.japanese:
いくつもの機関と人材を、怒り狂う民への生贄と
して捧げ、ようやく事態は沈静に傾いた。
　ついでに国連も傾いた。
lines.english: Only after several institutions and individuals were offered up as sacrifices to the furious public did the crisis begin to subside. The United Nations nearly toppled along with it.

lines.japanese:
これを機に国家同士の対立が顕著になり、人類史
普遍の節理として謀略が渦巻き、地球全体は変わら
ず生ぬるいものであり続けた。
lines.english: The incident brought interstate antagonisms into the open; plots swirled, as they always had throughout human history, and the world at large remained as tepid as ever.

lines.japanese:
最終的に敷設計画はアメリカ・日本の二国でのみ
細々と継続されることになる。
　責任の所在もまた、この二国に押しつけられた。
lines.english: Ultimately, the Deployment Plan survived only in the United States and Japan, and even there only in diminished form. Responsibility for it was thrust upon those two nations as well.

lines.japanese:
拒絶。
　人は保守的であり、拒絶するものである。
　ただ自分のみを肯定して生きる。
lines.english: Rejection. People were conservative by nature, and so they rejected. They lived by affirming themselves alone.

lines.japanese:
結果として、二国は大災厄に備え、秘密裏の計画
を推進することになった。
lines.english: As a result, the two nations secretly advanced a plan to prepare for the great calamity.

lines.japanese:
それは言い換えれば、二国だけが助かろうとする
構図でもある。
　そして民を欺く、閉じられた政策である。
lines.english: Put another way, it was an arrangement by which only those two nations would save themselves. A closed-door policy that deceived the public.

lines.japanese:
人は責めた。
　自分たちが排撃してのけた計画、その独占を責め
たのである。
lines.english: People condemned them. They condemned the two nations for monopolizing the very plan they themselves had driven out.

lines.japanese:
「様々な問題や対立をさ、超人的な手腕で鮮やかに
　解決して犠牲者なく大団円に導く……そんな奇跡
　の体現者が求められているんだ」
lines.english: “They want the embodiment of a miracle—someone who resolves every conflict and problem with superhuman brilliance, leading everyone to a happy ending without a single victim.”

lines.japanese:
「彼が非人道的な手段を取ることは、決して許され
　ない。隠されることも、等しく」
lines.english: “He can never be permitted to use inhumane means. Nor can those means be concealed.”

lines.japanese:
「法王庁がすぐに審査しに来るよ。奇跡を認定しに
　ね」
lines.english: “The Holy See would come investigate at once. To certify the miracle.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、そんな人間……いるわけないじゃないか」
lines.english: “But no such person… could possibly exist.”
“…………Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「誰だって、罪は背負いたくない」
lines.english: “No one wants to bear that sin.”

lines.japanese: 「だが、それが……王の責務だ」
lines.english: “But that is… a king's duty.”

lines.japanese: 真正面から、南は視線を投げつけた。
lines.english: Minami fixed him with a direct stare.

lines.japanese:
「王か。そう、そうだね。わかるよ。背負う覚悟は
　できてる。時間がかかったけど……できてるつも
　りだ」
lines.english: “A king. Yes… Yes, you're right. I understand. I'm prepared to carry it. It took me time… but I believe I'm ready.”

lines.japanese:
風が強さを増す。
　長髪が鼻先をかいて、南は目を細めた。
lines.english: The wind grew stronger. His long hair tickled his nose, and Minami narrowed his eyes.

lines.japanese:
「……だけど、終わったあと生きていたら……
　僕は……」
lines.english: “…But if I'm still alive when it's over… I…”

lines.japanese: 「皆、おまえに期待してる」
lines.english: “Everyone is counting on you.”

lines.japanese: 「怯えてるよ」
lines.english: “They're afraid of me.”

lines.japanese: 「失敗したら追求してやろうって、思っているかも」
lines.english: “They may be waiting to hold me to account if I fail.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことは……」
lines.english: “That's not…”

lines.japanese:
言いよどむ。
　確かに、そんな意識がないと言えば嘘だ。
　偏狭な能力者たちは、プライドばかりが高い。
lines.english: He faltered. It would be a lie to say there was no such sentiment. The narrow-minded USERs were nothing if not proud.

lines.japanese:
屈服させねば認めたりはしない。だが、力による
抑えつけは新たな不和の種でもある。
　南は言葉を吟味して、口にした。
lines.english: They would never acknowledge him until he forced them to submit. But suppressing them through force would plant new seeds of discord. Minami chose his words before speaking.

lines.japanese: 「俺は、おまえを責めたりはしない」
lines.english: “I will not condemn you.”

lines.japanese:
忍という存在に行き当たるまで辿った道筋に、南
は思いを馳せた。
lines.english: Minami thought back over the path that had led him to Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
現象行使者として調律された自分。
　力への目覚め。
　獲得と喪失。
lines.english: How he had been tuned into a wielder of phenomena. His awakening to power. What he had gained and lost.

lines.japanese:
絶望を知り、さまよい、ついに希望に至った。
　接触し、説得し、仕えるべき主君を得た。
lines.english: He had known despair, wandered, and finally reached hope. He had made contact, made his case, and found the lord he was meant to serve.

lines.japanese:
「……イマジナリー・ネットワークは、個々の行使
　者の性格や気持ちがどうであろうと……機能する
　ようになっていると聞いた」
lines.english: “…I heard that the Imaginary Network is designed to function no matter what personalities or feelings the individual wielders of phenomena may have.”

lines.japanese: 「本人の意志を無視してね」
lines.english: “By overriding each person's will.”

lines.japanese: 風が。
lines.english: The wind—

lines.japanese:
吹き巻いた。
　その強さに、南が腕で目を覆う。
　颶風が、二人に叩きつけられた。
lines.english: —whirled around them. Its force made Minami throw an arm across his eyes. A gale slammed into them both.

lines.japanese: 「忍……おまえの風なのか、これは……」
lines.english: “Shinobu… Is this your wind…?”

lines.japanese: うつむいたまま、忍は絞り出す。
lines.english: Still looking down, Shinobu forced the words out.

lines.japanese:
「僕はその気になれば、誰の聖域でも破壊できるじゃ
　ないか」
lines.english: “If I chose to, I could destroy anyone's sanctuary.”

lines.japanese: 「人々は、そんなものを許しはしない」
lines.english: “People will never forgive such a thing.”

lines.japanese:
「個の領域をもっとも尊重する、今という時代に……
　僕はいてはならないんだ」
lines.english: “In this age, when the realm of the individual is valued above all… I must not exist.”

lines.japanese: 「そこにいるだけで罪だから」
lines.english: “My very presence is a sin.”

lines.japanese: 「本当にそう思っているのか？　自分でも」
lines.english: “Is that really what you think? You yourself?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……自分でも、そう思うよ」
lines.english: “Yes… I believe it too.”

lines.japanese:
「僕は、罪深い王だ。最後のものとなるべき、統治
　者だ」
lines.english: “I am a sinful king. A ruler who ought to be the last of his kind.”

lines.japanese: 風の圧力が、ふっと消え去る。
lines.english: The pressure of the wind vanished abruptly.

lines.japanese:
南は見た。
　二人を中心として、小型の竜巻と化した風を。
　無風状態。
lines.english: Minami saw it. The wind had become a small tornado centered on the two of them. Within it, perfect stillness.

lines.japanese:
「……僕は、どんな裁きを受けることになるんだろ
　うな」
lines.english: “…I wonder what sort of judgment awaits me.”

lines.japanese: 「裁きなど」
lines.english: “What judgment could there be?”

lines.japanese: 南は眉をひそめる。
lines.english: Minami frowned.

lines.japanese: 「おまえは、大勢の人を救うかも知れないのに」
lines.english: “You may save a great many people.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうか」
lines.english: “…Right.”

lines.japanese: 竜巻が霧散した。
lines.english: The tornado dissolved.

lines.japanese: 「まだ計画が成功するか、わからなかったね」
lines.english: “We still don't know whether the plan will succeed.”

lines.japanese:
妙に明るい声だ。
　南も、薄皮一枚で背後に蠢く本音を、感じている。
lines.english: His voice was oddly bright. Minami too could feel Shinobu's true feelings writhing just beneath that thin surface.

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
「人は死滅するかも知れないし、生き残るかも知れ
　ない」
lines.english: “Humanity may perish. Or it may survive.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ」
lines.english: “That's right.”

lines.japanese: 励ますように、南は言う。
lines.english: Minami spoke as though offering encouragement.

lines.japanese: 「全ては……おまえにかかっている」
lines.english: “Everything… depends on you.”

lines.japanese: 「僕次第か」
lines.english: “On me.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、南」
lines.english: “Tell me, Minami.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese:
「もし僕が、人の意志を踏みにじってまで、こんな
　計画を実行することはできないと言ったら？」
lines.english: “What if I said I couldn't carry out a plan like this if it meant trampling over people's will?”

lines.japanese: 長い沈黙が降りてきた。
lines.english: A long silence descended.

lines.japanese: 「……僕を、殺す？」
lines.english: “…Would you kill me?”

lines.japanese: 「まさか」
lines.english: “Of course not.”

lines.japanese: 苦慮のためか、声は掠れていた。
lines.english: Perhaps from the strain of wrestling with it, his voice had gone hoarse.

lines.japanese:
「おまえを殺してどうする……
　そもそも、殺すことが現実問題としてできる
　のかどうか……」
lines.english: “What good would killing you do…? For that matter, could we actually kill you at all…”

lines.japanese:
「そう……データを見て気がついたことがある。
　おまえは……おまえの精神というものは……」
lines.english: “Yes… I noticed something when I looked at the data. You… Your mind, I mean…”

lines.japanese: 「それは僕にもわからないよ」
lines.english: “I don't know either.”

lines.japanese: 「あまり考えたことがないんだ」
lines.english: “I haven't given it much thought.”

lines.japanese:
「だがもし、おまえの心や魂というものが……
　その―――」
lines.english: “But if what we call your heart, or your soul… If it—”
“Minami!”

lines.japanese: 怒声に両断され、南の言葉は先細りに散った。
lines.english: The shout cut Minami's words in two; the rest trailed away.

lines.japanese: 「その言葉で、説明されても困る」
lines.english: “Don't try to define me in those terms.”

lines.japanese:
「だが……そう定義できることだ。おまえの存在は、
　元来想定されていた性能を遙かに凌駕している」
lines.english: “But… it can be defined that way. Your existence far surpasses the performance originally anticipated.”

lines.japanese: 「脳幹の完全蘇生など、不可能なことだ」
lines.english: “Complete regeneration of the brainstem is impossible.”

lines.japanese: 「記憶はどうやっても蘇生しようがないはずだ！」
lines.english: “There should be no way to restore memories!”

lines.japanese:
「つまりおまえは……奇跡の上に成立している存在
　ということだ」
lines.english: “Which means that your very existence… rests upon a miracle.”

lines.japanese: 「言っちゃった……」
lines.english: “You said it…”

lines.japanese:
時間が停止してしまったかのようだった。
　忍は小さく笑う。
lines.english: It was as though time itself had stopped. Shinobu gave a small laugh.

lines.japanese: 「だが、そうだ」
lines.english: “But it is true.”

lines.japanese: 「……まさか」
lines.english: “…No way.”

lines.japanese:
「奇跡だと思っていたものは、最初からありえたこ
　となんだよ」
lines.english: “What seemed like a miracle had been possible all along.”

lines.japanese: 「人が不完全だから、そういう部分を見落とすんだ」
lines.english: “Human beings overlook things like that because they're imperfect.”

lines.japanese:
「だがな、おまえに投じられた技術で説明するには、
　ＥＳセルだって記憶情報までは―――」
lines.english: “But the technology that went into you can't account for it. Even ES cells shouldn't be able to restore memory data—”

lines.japanese: 「……痛たたたた」
lines.english: “…Ow-ow-ow-ow.”
“Shinobu?”

lines.japanese: 額をいさめるように、拳で叩く。
lines.english: He rapped a fist against his forehead as though scolding it.

lines.japanese:
「いつもの頭痛……ここしばらく大人しかったのに、
　また来た」
lines.english: “My usual headache… It had behaved itself for a while, but now it's back.”
“Ah…”

lines.japanese: 気勢をそがれる南。
lines.english: The wind went out of Minami's sails.

lines.japanese: 「こりゃひどいな、鐘の真下にいるみたいだ」
lines.english: “This one's awful. Like standing right beneath a bell.”

lines.japanese: 「……医務室に行った方がいい」
lines.english: “…You should go to the infirmary.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだね」
lines.english: “Yeah. I should.”

lines.japanese:
一人、歩き出す。
　頭だけ振り返り、告げる。
lines.english: He set off alone. Turning only his head, he called back.

lines.japanese: 「蘇生したって、頭痛一つ取り去れない」
lines.english: “Even coming back from the dead couldn't cure one headache.”
“…Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「うん？」
lines.english: “Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「俺たちは、従えるには頼りないか？」
lines.english: “Are we too unreliable to serve under you?”

lines.japanese:
ぽつ、と。
　南はそんなことを口にした。
lines.english: The question fell softly. Minami had finally put it into words.

lines.japanese: 「何を言ってるの？」
lines.english: “What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese:
「今回のことで、俺たちはおまえの力を確認した。
　意志も」
lines.english: “This time, we saw your power for ourselves. And the strength of your will.”

lines.japanese:
「治癒能力を持つ全員が、いや、そうでない者も……
　外傷の治癒速度が異常にはやいと言っている。そ
　れも、おまえの仕業じゃないかという噂がある」
lines.english: “Everyone with healing abilities—and even those without—says their injuries are healing unnaturally fast. There's a rumor that it's your doing too.”

lines.japanese: 「ここ数日、誰か話しかけてきたか？」
lines.english: “Has anyone spoken to you these past few days?”

lines.japanese: 「いや」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 額を押さえる。
lines.english: He pressed a hand to his forehead.

lines.japanese: 「興味ないんじゃないのかな」
lines.english: “Maybe they're not interested.”

lines.japanese: 「違う。恐れている」
lines.english: “No. They fear you.”

lines.japanese: 「怯えられたってこと？」
lines.english: “I've frightened them?”

lines.japanese: 「違う。畏怖に近い。だが恐怖ではなく……その」
lines.english: “No. It is closer to awe. But not fear… It's…”

lines.japanese: 照れつつ、南は言った。
lines.english: Minami said it with some embarrassment.

lines.japanese: 「敬意だ」
lines.english: “Respect.”

lines.japanese: 一瞬、頭痛さえ忘れた。
lines.english: For one moment, he even forgot his headache.

lines.japanese:
「つまり、おまえが戦陣に立つことを、連中は認め
　たということだ。下で戦うことも」
lines.english: “It means they've accepted you leading them in battle. They've accepted fighting under your command, too.”

lines.japanese:
「内心気にくわない者もいるだろう。が、明確な反
　対者はもういない」
lines.english: “Some of them may still resent it privately. But no one openly opposes you now.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえしかできないと理解したからだ」
lines.english: “Because they understand that only you can do this.”

lines.japanese: 「俺も含めてな」
lines.english: “Myself included.”

lines.japanese: 「俺はおまえを守る。同じ人類の、未熟さ全てから」
lines.english: “I will protect you from all the failings of our fellow human beings.”

lines.japanese:
「権力も、毒殺も、狙撃も、不慮の事故も、近づけ
　させない」
lines.english: “Political power, poison, snipers, accidents—I will allow none of them near you.”

lines.japanese:
「任務だからそうするんじゃない。俺がすべきだと
　思うから、そうする」
lines.english: “I’m not doing this because it’s my mission. I’m doing it because I believe I should.”

lines.japanese: 「責任が重いのであれば、皆で背負おう」
lines.english: “If the weight of that responsibility is too much, we'll all shoulder it together.”

lines.japanese: 背筋を伸ばす。
lines.english: He drew himself up straight.

lines.japanese: 一分の隙もない、敬礼。忍に向けて。
lines.english: A flawless salute—offered to Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
「青木ヶ原ならびに軍艦島出身のＵＳＥＲ、南レイ
　以下残存１７名、ユニット・アウレリウス／貴宮忍
　の指揮下に入ります」
lines.english: “I, Rei Minami, and the 16 other surviving USERs of Aokigahara and Gunkanjima hereby place ourselves under the command of Unit Aurelius— Shinobu Atemiya.”

lines.japanese:
瞳を限界まで見開いて、忍は惚けた。
　言葉が脳にとけるのに、時間がかかった。
lines.english: Shinobu stared blankly, his eyes as wide as they would go. It took a moment for the words to sink in.

lines.japanese:
南の演技ぶった態度にも、底に流れる誠実さにも、
意識が遠のくほど目が眩んだ。
lines.english: Between Minami's theatrical bearing and the sincerity beneath it, Shinobu was so dazzled he nearly blacked out.

lines.japanese: 「ふふ」
lines.english: “Heh.”

lines.japanese:
そこにもまた、小さな共有があった。
　軽く表層をかすめただけの、小さな共感だ。
　深層の相互理解とはほど遠い。
lines.english: Here too, something small had been shared. A small moment of empathy, merely grazing the surface. Far removed from mutual understanding at the deepest level.

lines.japanese:
なのに、なぜ人は、そこに価値を見いだすのだろ
う？
lines.english: And yet why did people find value in it?

lines.japanese: 懸命に、見いだそうとするのだろう？
lines.english: Why did they strive so desperately to find it?

lines.japanese:
愚かで矮小な肯定。
　だが忍には、今の忍には、痛いほどよく理解できた。
lines.english: A foolish, paltry affirmation. But Shinobu—Shinobu as he was now—understood it so well it hurt.

lines.japanese: 「じゅーはっち名！」
lines.english: “Eighteeen!”

lines.japanese:
二人は、子供のようにビクッと肩を震わせた。
　そんなことで動じる二人ではない。
　が……相性が悪いらしい。
lines.english: Both of them jumped like children. Neither of them was easily shaken by something like that. But… apparently neither of them handled her very well.

lines.japanese: 「南レイ以下１８名、に訂正。私も参加する」
lines.english: “Correction: 18 under Rei Minami. I'm joining too.”

lines.japanese:
微笑みに敬礼を添えて、シャーリーが草むらから
立ち上がった。
lines.english: Smiling, Shirley saluted as she rose from the grass.

lines.japanese: 「なっ、君、どこから……？」
lines.english: “Wh-where did you come from…?”

lines.japanese:
「このあいだの一件から、ちょっと力が戻りました
　ゆえ、シールの実験をしておりました」
lines.english: “Some of my power has returned since that last incident, so I was conducting a test of Seal.”

lines.japanese: 隠蔽能力。
lines.english: A concealment ability.

lines.japanese: 「二人に気づかれず接近できたら成功」
lines.english: “If I could get this close without either of you noticing, the test was a success.”

lines.japanese: 「……気を抜きすぎたな」
lines.english: “…I let my guard down far too much.”

lines.japanese:
よほどショックだったのか、南は眉間をつねって
いた。
lines.english: Apparently rattled, Minami pinched the bridge of his nose.

lines.japanese:
忍はまだ、言葉を失っている。
　理由は南とは、異なる。
lines.english: Shinobu was still lost for words. For a reason different from Minami's.

lines.japanese:
風はもうない。
　沈殿していく、草原の凪。
lines.english: The wind was gone. Stillness settled over the grassland.

lines.japanese:
「本気で参加するのか？　君はもう引退している身
　だ。もっともつらい任務から生還して、一度は死
　から免れた。そんな幸運は二度も続かない」
lines.english: “Are you truly joining us? You're retired. You survived the harshest of assignments and escaped death once. Luck like that won't hold twice.”

lines.japanese: 「人手不足なんでしょ？」
lines.english: “You're short on people, aren't you?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだが……足抜けのチャンスだ」
lines.english: “We are, but… this is your chance to get out.”

lines.japanese:
「昔は、つらいと思ったこともあったけど……
　やっぱ良い上司に恵まれると、違うと思う」
lines.english: “I used to find it hard sometimes… but having good people in charge really does make a difference.”

lines.japanese: 「二人の下でなら、自分の意志で戦えそうだし」
lines.english: “Under the two of you, I think I could fight of my own free will.”

lines.japanese: 「シャーリー……俺は君を過小評価していたかな」
lines.english: “Shirley… Perhaps I underestimated you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でも爆弾はゴメンナサイです。死にたくない」
lines.english: “Oh, but no more bomb duty for me. I don't want to die.”

hyperlinks.preview: A form of phenomenal power classified under projection in derivative phenomenology.

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: A form of phenomenal power classified under projection in derivative phenomenology.

lines.japanese: 突きだした両手を、小刻みに振る。
lines.english: She held both hands out and waved them rapidly.

lines.japanese: 「そもそも、なくなっちゃったし」
lines.english: “It's gone now anyway.”

lines.japanese:
「ああ、現象行使者一人分の演算能力は常人の数人
　分だ。それだけでも、助かる」
lines.english: “Yes. One wielder of phenomena has the processing capacity of several ordinary people. That alone will help.”

lines.japanese: 「今度の敵は、対人能力は必要ないしな」
lines.english: “We won't need anti-personnel abilities against our next enemy.”

lines.japanese: 「力になれますね、たいちょ」
lines.english: “I can help, Cap.”

lines.japanese: 今の忍は、
lines.english: Shinobu, at that moment—

lines.japanese: 「…………馬鹿だな、君たちはッ……ッ！」
lines.english: “…………You idiots… Both of you…!”

lines.japanese:
とても二人の顔を見ることはできない。
　視線を地面に落として、だけど雫までは落とさな
いよう必死にまぶたを閉じ、
lines.english: He could not possibly look either of them in the face. He dropped his gaze to the ground and squeezed his eyes shut, desperate not to let the drops fall—

lines.japanese:
得体の知れない衝動に突き上げられながら、
　無形の何かに感謝を捧げた。
lines.english: —while some unknowable impulse surged through him, and he offered his thanks to something without form.

lines.japanese: 一撃（正確には二撃）で、ボロボロだった―――
lines.english: One blow—two, to be precise—had left him in tatters—

lines.japanese:
起きる。
　寝覚めの感触が、いつもと違っている。
　妙に、心が騒ぐ。
lines.english: He woke. Waking felt different than usual. His heart was strangely restless.

lines.japanese:
低調ではない。
　まるで、幸せな毎日を過ごしているかのよう
な―――
lines.english: He wasn't feeling low. If anything, it felt as though every day had been full of happiness—

lines.japanese: （……それはナイ）
lines.english: (…As if.)

lines.japanese:
いつもの癖で、自らを戒める。
　どんなショックにも落胆しないで済むよう。
lines.english: Out of habit, he admonished himself. A habit meant to spare him disappointment, no matter the shock.

lines.japanese: （けど）
lines.english: (But…)

lines.japanese:
口元がおかしい。
　触れてみる。
lines.english: Something felt odd around his mouth. He touched it.

lines.japanese:
あろうことか。
　自分は、にんまりしていたらしい。
lines.english: Unbelievable. Apparently he had been grinning.

lines.japanese: 「あああ」
lines.english: “Aaaagh.”

lines.japanese: 頭をかきむしる。
lines.english: He raked his fingers through his hair.

lines.japanese: 「ああああああああ」
lines.english: “Aaaaaaaaaagh.”

lines.japanese:
頭をかきむしる。
　そんな朝だった。
lines.english: He raked his fingers through his hair. That was the sort of morning it was.

lines.japanese: 一つ、ご機嫌の理由をでっちあげてみた。
lines.english: He tried making up a reason for his good mood.

lines.japanese: （悪夢……見なかったな）
lines.english: (I didn't… have a nightmare.)

lines.japanese:
ほとんど義務化していた夢。
　昨晩は、熟睡できたらしい。
　愕然とする。
lines.english: Those dreams had become almost obligatory. It seemed he had slept soundly last night. The realization stunned him.

lines.japanese: でっちあげたどころか、紛れもなく良い変化だ。
lines.english: Far from a fabrication, it was an unmistakably positive change.

lines.japanese:
章二のことで、どれだけでも苦しむつもりだった
のに。
lines.english: He had meant to keep suffering over Shouji, no matter how much it hurt.

lines.japanese: もう、自力では苦しめない気がした―――
lines.english: Now he felt he could no longer make himself suffer—

lines.japanese: そこは、奇妙な空間と化していた。
lines.english: The room had become a strange place.

lines.japanese:
千鳥。
　忍。
lines.english: Chidori. Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
南。
　邑西。
lines.english: Minami. Yuuzai.

lines.japanese:
その四人がいた。
　会話の弾むメンツではない。
　四人はそれぞれ、用事があってここにいる。
lines.english: All four were present. Not exactly a group given to lively conversation. Each was there on separate business.

lines.japanese:
そして同時に、わずかな時間のエアポケットに落
ち込んで、自室に引き上げることもできず待機を強
いられている。
lines.english: At the same time, all four had been caught in a brief pocket of dead time, unable to withdraw to their rooms and forced to wait.

lines.japanese: 邑西のコーヒーをすする音が、妙に響く。
lines.english: The sound of Yuuzai sipping coffee echoed with peculiar clarity.

lines.japanese: （……陰気だなぁ……）
lines.english: (…This is grim…)
(…Grim…)

lines.japanese: （……陰気だわ……）
lines.english: (…What a miserable atmosphere…)

lines.japanese: （……なんと陰気な……）
lines.english: (…Remarkably grim…)

lines.japanese:
同時に同じことを考えたりもする。
　個々の関係性が、以前と変わっているせいもある。
lines.english: They even found themselves thinking the same thing at once. Part of the reason was that their relationships with one another had changed.

lines.japanese:
千鳥と忍。
　忍と南。
　特にこの軸は、全交換されたに近い。
lines.english: Chidori and Shinobu. Shinobu and Minami. Those two axes in particular had been almost completely rewired.

lines.japanese: 忍は他の三人と、どう接していいかわからない。
lines.english: Shinobu no longer knew how to act around the other three.

lines.japanese:
千鳥や南にしても同様で、邑西はもともと忍には
ぎこちない。
lines.english: The same went for Chidori and Minami, while Yuuzai had always been awkward around Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
つまり、癌は忍だ。
　複雑な人間関係の渦中にいる忍が、一人退出すれ
ば空気は弛緩する。
lines.english: In short, Shinobu was the cancer. If Shinobu, at the center of that tangle of relationships, left the room alone, the atmosphere would relax.

lines.japanese:
これはそういう仕組みであった。
　机を囲み、世間話をするでもなく、飲み物を口に
する。
lines.english: That was how the mechanism worked. They sat around a table, drinking without so much as making small talk.

lines.japanese:
インスタント・コーヒーだ。
　決して美味いものではない。
　なのだが、消費は速い。
lines.english: Instant coffee. It was by no means good. Yet it vanished quickly.

lines.japanese:
気まずさが、カップの往復を早めていた。
　意を決してかどうか、忍と南が同時に口を開いた。
lines.english: Awkwardness kept the cups moving at a brisk pace. Perhaps they had both worked up the nerve: Shinobu and Minami spoke at once.
“Um—” “Um—”

lines.japanese:
そして再び沈黙が訪れた。
　何をやっているのやら。
lines.english: And silence descended once more. What were they doing?

lines.japanese: 「あ、そう、忍」
lines.english: “Oh, that reminds me, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「え、はい？」
lines.english: “Oh—yes?”

lines.japanese:
「あなたがつかまえた彼女、まだ閉じこめたままな
　んじゃないかしら？」
lines.english: “Isn't that woman you captured still locked away?”

lines.japanese: 「彼女？」
lines.english: “What woman?”

lines.japanese: 「……ジーンか？」
lines.english: “…Gene?”
“Oh—”

lines.japanese:
忍は内心、経過した日数を指折り数えた。
　そして蒼白になった。
lines.english: In his head, Shinobu counted off the days. Then he went white.

lines.japanese:
いかに王でも、飢え死にした人間を蘇生するのは
不可能だ。
lines.english: Even a king could not revive someone who had starved to death.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あっ、そんな……あ、ああ……」
lines.english: “Oh—oh, no… Oh…”

lines.japanese: うろたえる。
lines.english: He panicked.

lines.japanese: 「アレは、どうなんです？」
lines.english: “How is that thing?”

lines.japanese:
「シャーリーが食事だけは運んでいたようだけど……
　魂が抜けたみたいだったと」
lines.english: “Apparently Shirley has at least been bringing her meals… though she said the woman looked as if her soul had left her.”

lines.japanese:
「でしょうね。捕虜になって放置なんて、アレにし
　てみれば面白くない展開だ」
lines.english: “I imagine so. Being taken prisoner and then ignored cannot be an entertaining development for that thing.”

lines.japanese:
面白くない展開の影で、ほっと安堵している忍が
いる。
lines.english: While the others discussed this unentertaining turn of events, Shinobu was quietly breathing a sigh of relief.

lines.japanese: （シャーリー……君はヘンだけど最高だ）
lines.english: (Shirley… You're strange, but you're the best.)

lines.japanese:
「ジーン……そのセンスのないネーミングは、確か
　トレント博士の？」
lines.english: “Gene… That singularly tasteless name was, if I recall, Dr. Trent’s?”

lines.japanese:
「ええ。例の微細現象学の、極めて高純度の結合例
　だそうです」
lines.english: “Yes. Supposedly she is an exceptionally pure example of coupling in that field of microphenomenology.”

lines.japanese: 「興味深いな、データは？」
lines.english: “Fascinating. Do we have the data?”

lines.japanese: 「今度、お渡しします」
lines.english: “I'll give it to you later.”

lines.japanese:
「以前、論文を読んだことがあるが、あれこそまさ
　にケミカル技術の粋だ。細胞単位での念動などは、
　医療分野から不可能を除去するにも等しい」
lines.english: “I read a paper on it once. It is the very pinnacle of chemical technology. Telekinesis at the cellular level would be tantamount to removing the word impossible from medicine.”

lines.japanese: 「ジーンは、細かなコントロールができないんです」
lines.english: “Gene is incapable of fine control.”

lines.japanese:
「あくまでも理論的には可能ということらしいので
　すが」
lines.english: “In theory, at least, it should be possible.”

lines.japanese: 「かなり乱暴に使っているようです」
lines.english: “She seems to use it rather crudely.”

lines.japanese: 「その力は、有視界かね？」
lines.english: “Does the power require line of sight?”

lines.japanese:
「ええ、基本的には見ていないと使えない。ですか
　ら患部を見通す顕微鏡のようなものがなければ、
　実用化は難しいでしょう」
lines.english: “Yes. In principle, she cannot use it without seeing the target. So practical application would be difficult without something like a microscope capable of seeing into the affected area.”

lines.japanese: 「……非効率だ」
lines.english: “…Inefficient.”

lines.japanese:
「それでも、将来性のある技術には違いありません。
　トレント博士は、戦後のことを考えていろいろと
準備をされていると聞きました」
lines.english: “It remains a promising technology nonetheless. I have heard Dr. Trent is making various preparations for after the war.”

lines.japanese: 「ジーンへの手紙が、よく届けられていたようです」
lines.english: “Letters from him were apparently delivered to Gene quite often.”

lines.japanese: 邑西の顔が、曇る。
lines.english: Yuuzai's face clouded.

lines.japanese: 「戦後……か」
lines.english: “After the war…”

lines.japanese: 「ジーンのは、純粋念動に近いものですからね」
lines.english: “Gene's ability is close to pure telekinesis.”

lines.japanese:
「模倣子を介在しているにしても、個々の細胞に命令
　を発信するまでが従来の現象行使で、活動力自体は
　細胞自身のものを使っている」
lines.english: “Even with mimetic units acting as intermediaries, conventional phenomenon operation goes no further than transmitting instructions to individual cells. The cells themselves still provide the energy.”

lines.japanese: 「ということは遅効性だな」
lines.english: “Then its effects are delayed.”

lines.japanese:
「そうです。うまく作用させられれば、ある程度即
　効性も出るようですが……例えば、細胞の結合を
　解除する、とか」
lines.english: “Yes. If applied correctly, it can apparently produce effects almost immediately… by breaking the bonds between cells, for example.”

lines.japanese: 「それは君の力だろう？」
lines.english: “Is that not your own ability?”

lines.japanese:
「教えました。もっとも自分のはアレと違って、模
　倣子の誘発因子を用いて強制介入しているので、
　効果に差はあります」
lines.english: “I taught her. Unlike hers, however, mine uses a mimetic-unit trigger to force an intervention, so the resulting effect differs.”

lines.japanese: 「首は無理ですが、耳くらいならなんとか」
lines.english: “She couldn't manage a neck, but an ear is within reach.”

lines.japanese:
「強制力が働かないのであれば、細いものしか切断
　はできないか」
lines.english: “Without forced intervention, then, she can only sever thin targets.”

lines.japanese:
「ええ。内部まで浸透させるのが難しいですし、
　ジーンは骨には指示が出せない」
lines.english: “Yes. Reaching deep inside is difficult, and Gene cannot issue instructions to bone.”

lines.japanese:
「結果、ジーンが特化したのは、だから神経切断だ
　けなんです」
lines.english: “That is why Gene ended up specializing in one thing alone: severing nerves.”

lines.japanese: 「見えていないと作用させられないのでは？」
lines.english: “But I thought she could not act without seeing the target?”

lines.japanese:
「対象が見えていれば、人間の体ですから、神経の
　位置はわかります。皮膚や粘膜から命令を伝達し
　て、神経だけを麻痺させたり切ったり……」
lines.english: “As long as she can see the subject, she knows where the nerves are in a human body. She sends instructions through the skin and mucous membranes to paralyze or sever the nerves alone…”

lines.japanese: 「だからアレは、神経については詳しい」
lines.english: “That is why the thing knows so much about nerves.”

lines.japanese: 「彼女は作用にも優れていますね」
lines.english: “She’s also skilled in its application.”

lines.japanese:
「もともと遅効性の効果を加速するため、投射も併
　用しているんです。ただ彼女の弾丸化は付け焼き
　刃なので」
lines.english: “She combines it with projection to accelerate an effect that is naturally delayed. But her technique for turning it into projectiles is makeshift, so—”

lines.japanese:
「というかアレは努力が嫌いなので、あくまで牽制
　というレベルでしかありません」
lines.english: “Or rather, the thing hates effort. She never developed it beyond keeping opponents at bay.”

lines.japanese: 邑西が忍を見た。
lines.english: Yuuzai looked at Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 「どうやって捕獲したのかね？」
lines.english: “How did you capture her?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ああ、彼女は……その」
lines.english: “Oh—well, she… Um…”

lines.japanese:
快楽中毒。
　とは言えない。
lines.english: A pleasure addict. He could not say that.

lines.japanese: 「徒手格闘術をもって撃破しました」
lines.english: “I defeated her in unarmed combat.”

lines.japanese: 平気で嘘をつくこともある。
lines.english: Sometimes he could lie without a qualm.

lines.japanese: 「……防御だけしかできないのではなかったか？」
lines.english: “…I thought you could do nothing but defend?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、工夫して。ごほ……」
lines.english: “I improvised. Ahem…”

lines.japanese: 「風邪？」
lines.english: “A cold?”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほど、先手を打ったのだな」
lines.english: “I see. You struck first.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
「動物的直感を持つアレの不意をつけるとは、やる
　な忍」
lines.english: “You managed to catch that thing, with all its animal instincts, off guard. Not bad, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「いやまあ、天候とか、いろいろ」
lines.english: “Well, there was the weather and… various factors.”

lines.japanese: 「天候？　どんな関係が？」
lines.english: “The weather? What bearing did it have?”

lines.japanese: 「ごほん、げほん」
lines.english: “Ahem. Cough.”

lines.japanese:
千鳥が目を細めた。
　ここにいるメンツで、忍に対する理解は彼女が
一番深い。
lines.english: Chidori narrowed her eyes. Of everyone there, she understood Shinobu best.

lines.japanese: 小さく、ため息をついた。そして、
lines.english: She gave a quiet sigh. Then—

lines.japanese: 「では、そろそろ交渉した方がいいのでは？」
lines.english: “Then perhaps it is time to negotiate with her?”

lines.japanese: 「そうですね。自分も行きます」
lines.english: “Yes. I'll come too.”

lines.japanese: 「交渉？」
lines.english: “Negotiate?”

lines.japanese:
「こちらに戻るか、本国に送還されるか。本人に決
　めてもらうさ」
lines.english: “She can return to our side or be repatriated. We'll let her decide.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、罪には問われないんだ」
lines.english: “Oh. So she won't be charged with anything.”

lines.japanese:
「動機が明白すぎるからな。あれは……楽しいこと
　だけしていたいんだ」
lines.english: “Her motive is far too obvious. That thing… only wants to do what she finds fun.”

lines.japanese: 「政治的意図なんてない。断言できる」
lines.english: “She has no political intent whatsoever. I can guarantee it.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほど……」
lines.english: “I see…”

lines.japanese: つきあいが長いだけあって、南の言には重みがある。
lines.english: Their long association lent Minami's words weight.

lines.japanese: 少し、はた迷惑さをまとわりつかせた、重み。
lines.english: A weight tinged with just how much trouble she caused everyone around her.

lines.japanese: 「…………英雄色を好む」
lines.english: “…………Great men have great appetites.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、何か言いましたか？」
lines.english: “Sorry, did you say something?”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ、何も」
lines.english: “No. Nothing.”

lines.japanese: （しかし、ジーンか）
lines.english: (Still… Gene.)

lines.japanese:
戦いより『楽しい』ことがあれば、放棄してしま
うのも道理である。
lines.english: If she found something more “fun” than fighting, it made perfect sense that she would abandon the battle.

lines.japanese: 自分の体質に責任があるとはいえ、しかし―――
lines.english: His own constitution might have been responsible, but even so—

lines.japanese: 懊悩する忍を、千鳥は一度だけ、横目で見た。
lines.english: Chidori gave the anguished Shinobu a single sidelong glance.

lines.japanese: そのときに彼女が何を思ったのかは、伏せておこう。
lines.english: What passed through her mind then, we shall leave unsaid.

lines.japanese: 野暮というものだ。
lines.english: To say it would be hopelessly gauche.

lines.japanese: 「交渉というのは、どうするのかな？」
lines.english: “How are you planning to negotiate?”

lines.japanese:
「……まあ、金とか自由時間とか、そのあたりだな。
　つきあいが長い分、俺の権限も知り尽くしているだ
　ろうし、無茶がきかないのもわかっているはずだ」
lines.english: “…Money, free time, things of that sort. We've known each other long enough that she knows the limits of my authority, and she should understand that unreasonable demands won't work.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、なら楽な交渉かな」
lines.english: “I see. Then this should be easy enough.”

lines.japanese:
「正直、アレは戦線離脱を希望するかも知れない。
　可能性は高い」
lines.english: “Honestly, that thing may ask to leave the front. There's a good chance.”

lines.japanese: 「……うん、わかる。そういう人だね」
lines.english: “…Yes, I can see that. That's the kind of person she is.”

lines.japanese:
「敵を倒すのは好きだったらしいが……おまえと立
　ち会う者の常として、自身の限界を確認させられ
　るだろう」
lines.english: “She apparently liked defeating enemies… but, like everyone who faces you, she will have had to confront her own limits.”

lines.japanese: 「戦いは楽しいことではなくなった、と」
lines.english: “So fighting stopped being fun.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうことだ」
lines.english: “Exactly.”

lines.japanese: ジーンを拘留している部屋に着く。
lines.english: They reached the room where Gene was being detained.

lines.japanese:
なお忍らには警察権が一部付与されているため、
拘留という言葉の用法は現在適切である。
lines.english: For the record, Shinobu and the others had been granted limited police powers, so “detained” was technically the correct word.

lines.japanese:
「そういえば……この施設の立場って、どうなって
　るんだろう？」
lines.english: “Come to think of it… where does this facility stand now?”

lines.japanese:
「ネットで調べなかったのか？　灰野たちの失敗で、
　政府は掌を返したさ。見事なほどにな」
lines.english: “You didn't check online? Haino and his people failed, so the government did a complete about-face. Spectacularly so.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、なんだ」
lines.english: “I… see.”

lines.japanese:
「万難は排された。あとは揃えられるだけ戦力を整
　えることだ」
lines.english: “Every obstacle has been removed. All that remains is to assemble as much fighting strength as we can.”

lines.japanese: 無造作に、南は個室の扉をあけた。
lines.english: Without ceremony, Minami opened the door to the private room.

lines.japanese:
「ねー、ちょっとー！　いい加減にしてよー！
　殺す気ー！？　死ぬって、本当に、死ぬ、
　死んじゃうって！　わかってんの？」
lines.english: “Heeey! Come on! Enough already! Are you trying to kill me?! I'm gonna die! Seriously, I'll die— I'm dying here! You got that?!”

lines.japanese:
「実際体おかしい。というか、暴れたい。体が疼い
　たあかつきには暴れたい。アメリカ人の９５％が
　フィットネス中毒って知らないの？」
lines.english: “My body’s seriously acting up. I mean, I want to go wild. When it starts itching like this, I want to go wild. Don’t you know 95 percent of Americans are fitness addicts?”

lines.japanese:
「刑務所だって中庭とか散歩させてくれんじゃん。
　何もないしここ。テレビテレビ、あと漫画、ゲーム
　も。絶対必要。娯楽必要」
lines.english: “Even prisons let you walk around a yard. There's nothing in here. TV. TV. And manga. Games too. Absolutely essential. I need entertainment.”

lines.japanese:
「メガネ持ってこい。顔の一部。ねえ、サムライアン
　の最新刊出てんだろ。１８巻。いいから黙ってもっ
　てこいや。金おまえ持ちで。あと話し相手」
lines.english: “Bring me my glasses. They're part of my face. Hey, the new Samurai-an is out, right? Volume 18. Shut up and bring it to me. You're paying. And bring me someone to talk to.”

lines.japanese:
「なんかしょぼいヤツでいいから。相田とか。とにか
　く暇潰すものもってこい」
lines.english: “Anyone lame will do. Aida or somebody. Just bring me something to kill time.”

lines.japanese:
「虐待だっつーのこんなの。これ以上続けるようなら
　明日からいじめるよ？」
lines.english: “This is abuse, is what it is. Keep it up and I'll start bullying you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 「相田は潰れた」
lines.english: “Aida was crushed.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、南だ」
lines.english: “Oh, it's Minami.”

lines.japanese: 「静まれ、ジーン」
lines.english: “Quiet, Gene.”

lines.japanese: 「だーってさー！」
lines.english: “But come ooon!”

lines.japanese:
「いっちゃなんだけどうちの博士、けっこー権力もっ
　てっからね？　あとでほんっとひどいよ？」
lines.english: “I don't like to brag, but our doctor has some serious influence, you know? You're gonna be in so much trouble later.”

lines.japanese:
「だいたい……え、相田潰れたの？
　死んだ？　死んじゃった？」
lines.english: “Anyway… Wait, Aida got crushed? He died? Is he dead?”

lines.japanese:
「死んではいない。だが重傷だ。全治三ヶ月。足も
　取れた。もう実戦は無理だな」
lines.english: “He isn't dead, but he is badly wounded. Three months to recover. He lost a leg too. He won't see combat again.”

lines.japanese: 「うっそ。誰がやったの？」
lines.english: “No way. Who did it?”

lines.japanese: 「俺だ」
lines.english: “I did.”

lines.japanese:
「……なんだ、南か。まあ順当な結果だな。
　ばっかだなぁ、南殺すなら毒殺がいいって話して
　たのに」
lines.english: “…Oh, Minami. Then that's about what you'd expect. Idiot. We said poison was the way to kill you.”

lines.japanese: 「俺を殺す手段を検討するのをやめろ」
lines.english: “Stop discussing ways to kill me.”

lines.japanese:
「ねー、頼むよー、ここ暇すぎ。死ぬ。狂う。出し
　てけろ。おねげーします。ごめんなさいもうしま
　せん」
lines.english: “Pleeease, it's way too boring in here. I'll die. I'll go crazy. Let me ooout. Pretty please. I'm sorry. I'll never do it again.”

lines.japanese: 頭をさげた。
lines.english: She bowed her head.

lines.japanese:
ストレスは本当らしく、１０円ハゲが一つできて
いた。
lines.english: The stress appeared genuine; she had developed a bald patch the size of a 10-yen coin.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ次第だ」
lines.english: “That is up to you.”

lines.japanese: 「ふあ？」
lines.english: “Wha?”

lines.japanese:
「主導権はこちらに取り戻した。政府も制圧に失敗
　し、屈服した。忍も起動状態に入った」
lines.english: “We have regained the initiative. The government's suppression attempt failed, and it has capitulated. Shinobu has entered an active state as well.”

lines.japanese: ジーンは忍を見やる。
lines.english: Gene looked toward Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
「……なるほど。政府にしてみれば、逆にお慈悲ー
　な状況か」
lines.english: “…I get it. So now the government is begging for mercy instead.”

lines.japanese: 「素直に謝罪なんてしてこなかったんでしょ？」
lines.english: “They didn't just come out and apologize, did they?”

lines.japanese:
「人身御供だな。手違いがあって一部、暴走があっ
　たと言ってきた。何人かの要人の首が飛んだ」
lines.english: “Scapegoats. They claimed there’d been a mix-up and some people had acted out of line. Several high-ranking heads rolled.”

lines.japanese: 「うひゃひゃ、笑える」
lines.english: “Ahahaha! That's hilarious.”

lines.japanese:
「おまえはどうする、もう一度こちらにつくか？
　それとも本国に帰るか？」
lines.english: “What will you do? Join us again, or return to your country?”

lines.japanese: 「その二者択一かぁ」
lines.english: “Those are my only two choices, huh?”

lines.japanese:
「当然だが、送還となったら準備に時間がかかる。
　当分、ここで留め置かれるぞ」
lines.english: “Naturally, repatriation will take time to arrange. You’ll be held here for a while yet.”

lines.japanese: ジーンは真底、嫌な顔をする。
lines.english: Gene looked genuinely appalled.

lines.japanese: 「……それは勘弁」
lines.english: “…Hard pass.”

lines.japanese:
「一応、僕からも頼むよ。今は一人でも志願者が必
　要なんだ」
lines.english: “I'll ask you too, for what it's worth. Right now we need every volunteer we can get.”

lines.japanese: と、ジーンは忍をひどく真面目な顔で見つめた。
lines.english: Gene gave Shinobu an intensely serious look.

lines.japanese: 見つめて、唸った。
lines.english: She kept staring and gave a thoughtful hum.

lines.japanese: 「うーん」
lines.english: “Hmmmm.”

lines.japanese: 「どうかな」
lines.english: “Well?”

lines.japanese:
「いくらダーリンの頼みでもねぇ。
　ちょっと複雑だな」
lines.english: “Even if it's my darling asking… it's complicated.”

lines.japanese: 「何を言っている」
lines.english: “What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「ダーリンなんだよねー？」
lines.english: “You are my darling, riiight?”

lines.japanese: 無邪気に同意を求めてくる。
lines.english: She innocently asked him to agree.

lines.japanese: 「と言っているが？」
lines.english: “What do you say to that?”

lines.japanese: 「ダーリン的行為にふけったものねー？」
lines.english: “We indulged in some darling-type activities, didn't we?”

lines.english: “Shinobu?”

lines.japanese: 「はじめて見る女だ」
lines.english: “I've never seen this woman before.”

lines.japanese: 嘘ついた。
lines.english: He lied.

lines.japanese: 「何ぃ？」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: 「ダーリングの痕跡は、隠せない」
lines.english: “There’s no hiding the traces of our darling-ing.”

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: Gene

lines.japanese: 首筋を見せる。
lines.english: She bared her neck.

lines.japanese: 「ほら、キスマーク」
lines.english: “See? A hickey.”

lines.japanese: 「ＳＩＮＯＢＵ！！」
lines.english: “SHINOBU!!”

lines.japanese:
「違うんだ、あれは僕であって僕じゃない……
　違う僕なんだ！　おかしいんだ、本心じゃない！
　本当だ！　自分でもわからないんだ！」
lines.english: “You've got it wrong! That was me, but it wasn't me… It was a different me! Something was wrong—I didn't mean it! I swear! I don't understand it either!”

lines.japanese:
「おまえというヤツは……
　まさか、戦闘中にそんなッッッ！！」
lines.english: “You… Don't tell me you did that in the middle of combat!!”

lines.japanese:
「別の場所にもあります。すごく好きな人じゃない
　と、なかなか見せられないところ」
lines.english: “There are marks in other places too. Places you can't really show anyone unless you like them very, very much.”
“  BLADE!!   HEART!!  ”

lines.japanese: 重層的に南は叫んだ。縦に読むほど慟哭だった。
lines.english: Minami cried out in layers. Blade above heart—刃 over 心—made 忍, Shinobu. Read from top to bottom, it was a wail.

lines.japanese: 「その僕は偽物なんだ！！」
lines.english: “That version of me was an impostor!!”

lines.japanese: 「そんな馬鹿なことがあるか！！」
lines.english: “How could that possibly be true?!”

lines.japanese: 「楽しいなぁ」
lines.english: “This is fun.”

lines.japanese: ひっかきまわして、ご満悦。
lines.english: Delighted with the chaos she had caused.

lines.japanese: 紆余曲折ありはしたものの、
lines.english: After some twists and turns—

lines.japanese: 「んじゃまあ、改めてよろしく！」
lines.english: “Well then—nice to be working with you again!”

lines.japanese: ジーン参戦―――
lines.english: Gene joins the fight—
